speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and relief with rest is very telling. Given your diplopia that changes with gaze direction and the proximal limb weakness, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of gaze-dependent diplopia, fluctuating muscle weakness that worsens with activity, and the absence of sensory deficits or recent infection strongly points to this diagnosis, likely with involvement of the ocular, bulbar, and limb muscles.
